title: Kyverna ‘resetting conversation’ with 1-year miv-cel data as autoimmune CAR-T peers hit safety snags
summary: As two Big Pharma players in the autoimmune CAR-T space face unexpected safety setbacks, Kyverna Therapeutics is reporting long-term clinical data that showcase sustained efficacy alongside an unblemished safety profile for its potential first-in-class candidate, miv-cel.

title: Lilly puts up $100M, plus billions on the backend, to form 5-target deal with China's InnoCare
summary: Eli Lilly has committed $100 million in upfront and near-term payments to InnoCare Pharma to form a five-target drug discovery pact. The deal features up to $3.25 billion in milestones.

title: Enveda reaps $311M series E to feed ambition to become a ‘household name’
summary: Enveda has raised a $311 million series E round, positioning the nature-derived drug discovery company to pursue its goal of becoming a household name over the next decade.

title: Trump's Department of War bets $47M on Flagship biotechs to develop countermeasures
summary: The Department of War has awarded Flagship Pioneering $47 million to develop medical countermeasure technologies against emerging threats.

title: Immunovant ends cutaneous lupus program after phase 2 flop
summary: Immunovant has stopped development of IMVT-1402 in cutaneous lupus erythematosus after failing a midphase test, closing off one path to market for the anti-FcRn antibody.

title: Boehringer adds $250M to value of Variant pact by expanding into cardiovascular disease
summary: Boehringer Ingelheim has dived deeper into its collaboration with Variant Bio by expanding the collaboration to cover cardiovascular disease to the tune of $250 million.

title: GSK aiming to ‘balance West and East’ after Hansoh deal success showed China’s potential
summary: GSK has been operating a strategy of “balancing the West and the East” since the Big Pharma’s eyes were opened to the potential of licensing drugs from China two years ago, according to an executive.

title: Roche’s phase 3 win tees up fight with Novartis for blockbuster kidney disease market
summary: Roche has reported a phase 3 win for sefaxersen in kidney disease, teeing up talks with regulators about the path to approval for the Ionis-partnered, would-be blockbuster candidate.

title: Anaconda Biomed snares $56M in funding for endovascular tech
summary: Medtech startup Anaconda Biomed has hauled in $53 million to help finish off work on a pivotal trial for its endovascular project.

title: Novartis secures new radioligand in $900M deal as competition strengthens
summary: As an imposing new competitor begins to take shape, radiopharma leader Novartis has beefed up its pipeline by licensing a preclinical radioligand therapy from a specialist Chinese biotech.

title: Celldex monoclonal antibody rebounds with pair of phase 3 wins for chronic skin condition
summary: Celldex touted a double phase 3 trial win in patients with treatment-refractory chronic spontaneous urticaria.

title: Amgen’s Horizon-acquired fusion protein eases Sjögren's severity in ph. 3 win
summary: An investigational drug for the autoimmune condition Sjögren's disease has scored a phase 3 win for Amgen, marking a positive sign for the Horizon Therapeutics-acquired pipeline that has so far struggled to gain traction.

title: Vertex’s midstage data amplify kidney disease market opportunity
summary: Vertex has reported positive phase 2b data for its kidney disease prospect inaxaplin, boosting its efforts to expand beyond the population targeted in a pivotal trial.

title: Lexeo takes up the Mantle in $8M acquisition for Friedreich ataxia assets
summary: Lexeo Therapeutics has agreed to acquire Mantle Therapeutics via an upfront payment of $8.3 million, aiming to expand its Friedreich ataxia (FA) portfolio while locking in three strategic collaborations to support its lead asset.

title: Otsuka heads to FDA as Ionis-partnered ALS drug hits primary phase 3 endpoint
summary: A phase 3 study of Otsuka and Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ amyotrophic lateral sclerosis drug candidate has hit its primary endpoint, positioning the partners to talk to regulators about expedited approvals.

title: Siemens Healthineers and Novo team up on fatty liver disease awareness, testing
summary: Siemens Healthineers is joining forces with Novo to help boost awareness and diagnosis of fatty liver disease.

title: Cordis’ sirolimus drug-coated balloon earns FDA approval as a breakthrough device
summary: The FDA gave the green light to a first and only sirolimus drug-eluting balloon designed by Cordis to treat coronary in-stent restenosis.

title: Boehringer, Envisagenics sign $1B multi-target oncology collaboration
summary: Boehringer Ingelheim and AI drug discovery company Envisagenics have agreed to a potential $1 billion multi-year pact that will task Boehringer with validating tumor-specific targets.

title: Roche’s GLP-1/GIP drug hits in phase 2 diabetes trial, fueling best-in-disease hopes
summary: A phase 2 trial of Roche’s dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist has hit its primary endpoints, painting the drug candidate as a potential treatment for people with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity.

title: Iambic maintains momentum from string of Big Pharma partnerships by aiming for IPO
summary: Iambic Therapeutics is maintaining the momentum generated by its recent mega round and Big Pharma partnerships by gearing up to go public.

title: White House plans to put NIH grants under political control: reports
summary: President Donald Trump is attempting to seize further control of funding decisions made by the National Institutes of Health. According to multiple reports, senior officials met in the Oval Office on Friday to discuss plans for an executive order that would create an external panel with the power to shoot down NIH grants.

title: Novo struggles to appease restive investors with consumer plans, blockbuster ambitions
summary: With reports leaking out of investor discontent, CEO Mike Doustdar opened Novo's Capital Markets Day by acknowledging that the company’s leadership “have to convince” the audience that “there is a bright future for Novo.”

title: China targets 25% share of global first-in-class drugs in new 5-year plan
summary: China is aiming to account for at least 25% of first-in-class drugs as part of a five-year push to cement its emerging status as a hotbed for innovative R&D.

Reconciling global collaboration and data sovereignty in neuroscience
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02468-wTension exists between the need for an open science culture and data sovereignty in global brain research. Ray et al. propose practical mechanisms for secure and equitable international collaboration.

title: Massively parallel assessment of gene regulatory activity at human cortical-structure-associated variants
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02454-2A large-scale functional screen identified noncoding variants that regulate gene activity during human brain development, providing insights into the molecular mechanisms that shape differences in human cortical structure.

title: Tibial bone compression promotes recovery after brain injury through osteocyte PIEZO1
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 21 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02422-wMechanical loading of the tibia improves survival and recovery after brain surgery in mice and pigs. This bone–brain axis is mediated by osteocyte PIEZO1, which triggers the release of neuroprotective factors into the circulation.

title: Reciprocal connections dynamically build consensus between neocortical areas
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02437-3The authors show that reciprocal interactions between cortical areas generate slow dynamics that gradually build consensus across distributed cortical networks, revealing a potential general principle for coordinating activity across the neocortex.

title: Serotonin neurons in the dorsal raphe control food-craving-like behavior during pregnancy in mice
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02445-3Zhao, Feng, Dong and colleagues found that pregnant mice crave highly palatable foods due to SK3-mediated inhibition of 5-HT neurons in DRN. Reactivating serotonergic DRN→VTA projections reduced these cravings and may provide new approaches to prevent maternal obesity.

title: Two parallel neural ectoderm progenitors contribute to the developing brain
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02433-7This study shows that the brain arises from two distinct progenitors: one forms the forebrain and midbrain, whereas the other generates the hindbrain. These insights enable the generation of human hindbrain motor neurons from pluripotent stem cells.
